Bill.BriefDescription: Addressing payments for medicaid contracted services in boarding homes.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to payments for medicaid contracted services inboarding homes; adding a new section to chapter 74.39A RCW; andproviding an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 74.39A RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Beginning July 1, 2008, the rates of payment for boarding homemedicaid contracted service under chapter 74.39 RCW and this chaptershall be established by the department, using the assisted living,adult residential care, and enhanced adult residential care sections ofthe "home and community rates model," developed by the department andpublished on November 22, 2006. The "home and community rates model"shall be updated using the 2005 nursing home cost report data,occupational employment statistics wage data from the Washingtonemployment security department and United States bureau of laborstatistics, and data from Marshall Swift valuation service to estimatethe cost of care for assisted living, enhanced adult residential care,and adult residential care services. The payment rates establishedunder this subsection shall reflect: p. 1 HB 3199 (a) Comprehensive assessment reporting evaluation classificationgroups and geographic areas in accordance with the applicable boardinghome sections of the "home and community rates model"; and (b) Adjustment by an economic trends and conditions factor whichshall be determined by the percentage change in the medical carecomponent of the consumer price index for all urban consumers from theindex of the month ending June 30th, from the year two yearsimmediately preceding the rate period to the index of the month endingJune 30th, from the year one year immediately preceding the rate periodfrom the data provided by the United States bureau of labor statistics;so that, for the rate period commencing July 1, 2008, the adjustmentfor economic trends and conditions is the calculated percentage changeof the index from the month ending June 30, 2006, compared to the indexfor the month ending June 30, 2007. (2) Beginning July 1, 2009, and thereafter for each odd-numberedyear beginning on July 1st, the rates of payment for boarding homemedicaid contracted services under chapter 74.39 RCW and this chaptershall be established by the department, using the assisted living,adult residential care, and enhanced adult residential care sections ofthe "home and community rates model," developed by the department andpublished on November 22, 2006. The "home and community rates model"shall be updated using the nursing home cost report data, occupationalemployment statistics wage data from the Washington employment securitydepartment and United States bureau of labor statistics, and data fromMarshall Swift valuation service to estimate the cost of care forassisted living, enhanced adult residential care, and adult residentialcare services from the year two years immediately preceding the rateperiod; so that, data from 2007 is used for July 1, 2009, through June30, 2011, boarding home payment rates; data from 2009 is used for July1, 2011, through June 30, 2013, boarding home payment rates; and soforth. The payment rates established under this subsection shallreflect: (a) Comprehensive assessment reporting evaluation classificationgroups and geographic areas in accordance with the applicable boardinghome sections of the "home and community rates model"; and (b) Adjustment by an economic trends and conditions factor whichshall be the lower of a factor determined by the percentage change inthe SeattleTacomaBremerton consumer price index from the actual HB 3199 p. 2 averaged index of the year, from the year two years immediatelypreceding the rate period to the forecasted average index of the yearof the rate period from the data provided by the Washington stateeconomic and revenue forecast council, as is published in theirquarterly state economic and revenue forecast for the quarter endingJune 30th, one year immediately preceding the rate period; or sixpercent; so that, for the rate period commencing July 1, 2009, theadjustment for economic trends and conditions is the lower of thecalculated percentage change of the actual index from the year 2007,compared to the forecasted index for the year 2009, or six percent. (3) Beginning July 1, 2010, and for all assisted living, enhancedadult residential care, and adult residential care services, ratesestablished on each subsequent July 1st occurring in even-numberedyears, the June 30th rate shall be adjusted by a factor determined bythe percentage change in the SeattleTacomaBremerton consumer priceindex from the forecasted index of the year, from the year two yearsimmediately preceding the rate period to the forecasted index of theyear from the year one year immediately preceding the rate period fromthe data provided by the Washington state economic and revenue forecastcouncil, as is published in their quarterly state economic and revenueforecast for the quarter ending June 30th, two years immediatelypreceding the rate period; so that, for the rate period commencing July1, 2010, the adjustment for economic trends and conditions is thecalculated percentage change of the forecasted index from the year2008, compared to the forecasted index for the year 2009; and so forth. (4) If any of the indices in subsection (1), (2), or (3) of thissection are unavailable, the department is permitted to substitute anavailable index.
